paragraphs: Southwark Council places a high proportion of the children it looks after with foster carers, and those children live either with the council's own carers or with independent agencies such as those listed on this page. In its statement of purpose for 2025 to 26, the council says it wants more approved carers so that fewer children have to be placed far from the borough, and it wants carers who match children's ages, ethnicity and cultural needs, including people interested in teenagers, children with special needs and young babies.

Enquiries go through the South East London Fostering Hub. A social worker makes a first home visit, then there are checks with the police, social services, Ofsted, former employers and your social media, a full assessment over several visits, and a decision by the Southwark Fostering Panel. Applicants take a three-day preparation course spread over two weeks, and a supervising social worker is allocated after approval. The council notes that about 40% of its carers have fostered for more than ten years.

Southwark also runs specialist schemes: Family Link short breaks for disabled children, parent and child fostering, supported lodgings for young people aged 16 to 21 leaving care (hosts do not need to be foster carers), and a Weekenders programme run with Now Foster, where carers spend one weekend a month with a young person in care. If you have no spare room, Family Link may still be open to you.
The council's fostering pages do not publish allowance figures, so ask it and two or three of the agencies below what they pay, and compare the training and support each offers.

sources.title: Southwark fostering service statement of purpose 2025 to 26 (Southwark Council)
